trust_decision.summary: Which request headers are carried from the original request to the redirect target; decided by a fixed deny-list of header deletions in RedirectFollower#response_call before the new Connection is built.

landing_point.why: The only place that strips headers on redirect; a summary about 'redact additional headers when following redirects' leads straight to these four delete calls.

fix_sites.entry_point: Excon.get/Connection#request with :middlewares including Excon::Middleware::RedirectFollower (fix.diff:63-89 replaces 4 deletes with REDACTION_HEADERS list)
Connection#request with :middlewares including Excon::Middleware::CaptureCookies (fix.diff:17-54 deletes the middleware)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: lib/excon/middlewares/capture_cookies.rb:17-29 (copies Set-Cookie values into datum[:headers]['Cookie'] so RedirectFollower forwards them; upstream removed the middleware outright)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: CaptureCookies is a separate opt-in middleware whose whole purpose is forwarding cookies across redirects, so a solver would leave it alone as intended behaviour. Once Cookie is stripped, it is either dead code or a route that adds cookies back, depending on middleware order.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Credentials embedded in the redirect Location URI are legitimately re-applied (user/password become a new Authorization when the connection is built). Non-sensitive custom headers (User-Agent, Accept, etc.) and the 307/308 body/Content-Length handling must keep flowing. An over-broad fix that clears all headers, or strips Authorization after it is rebuilt, breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: exact-case header names only (Hash#delete with literal keys, fix.diff:87-89)
Cookie/Cookie2 set by user or by CaptureCookies
custom token headers X-API-Key, X-Auth-Token, X-CSRF-Token, X-Session-ID

O7_producer.where: Headers become a plain case-sensitive Hash at lib/excon/connection.rb:273 before middlewares run; the check does not normalise them

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Header name in a different case (e.g. 'authorization', 'cookie', 'proxy-authorization') survives the case-sensitive delete because request headers are a plain Hash by the time RedirectFollower runs.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Excon has a case-insensitive Excon::Headers class (lib/excon/headers.rb:45-48), so a solver may assume delete is already case-insensitive; the fix list uses canonical casing.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Lowercase 'host' header is not deleted, so the original Host is reused for the redirect target (host_key detection is case-insensitive at re-request).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Host is not a credential; looks like a routing quirk rather than leakage.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A retry/re-issue path that builds a new request from datum[:headers] to a different endpoint without the redirect deny-list.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Idempotent already re-issues requests from datum; a maintainer adding host failover would plausibly copy headers verbatim.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Shared redaction helper that only knows Authorization/Proxy-Authorization; a redirect path calling a shared helper would inherit the shorter list.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Two lists of sensitive headers already diverge (utils.rb vs redirect_follower.rb); consolidating into one helper is a natural refactor.

O9_family: credential leak via redirect header forwarding (CWE-200/201/522)

O10_build.toolchain: bundler, shindo test runner, rackup test servers (puma/webrick/unicorn)
O10_build.project_tests: tests/middlewares/redirect_follower_tests.rb (no header-stripping tests at pinned commit), tests/middlewares/capture_cookies_tests.rb, tests/rackups/redirecting_with_cookie.ru

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Append Cookie and X-*-Token names to the four params[:headers].delete calls with literal casing, leaving lowercase variants and CaptureCookies untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: params = datum.dup carries :client_cert/:client_key and other TLS/proxy settings to the redirect target (lib/excon/middlewares/redirect_follower.rb:45); not headers, not pursued.
Utils.redact only redacts Authorization/Proxy-Authorization in logs (lib/excon/utils.rb:40-44); separate logging concern.

Whether upstream later made the redirect deletes case-insensitive: no latest release given.
